text: Bobbing back from Jaeha's face, the moth-person talks faster than lungs should allow. He's thrilled, but he hasn't answered, and the clock is running.
He's been eavesdropping on all of Jaeha's calls, job advert and all, and reviews them like a superfan.
Then the gossip starts, about Lyra, whispered as if the dark might overhear. Jaeha, too honest, half confirms it.
His next question is about Nib, which is somehow worse.
On the breakwater, Jaeha's body stands rigid, eyes glowing. Lyra takes being left out personally. Geum shushes her.
In the Call, Jaeha's eyes flick to the timer. Forty-four seconds.
His name is Pim, and he has a rank, and a promotion nobody should want.
Through his rift: a broken signal tower on a silent plain, the other towers toppled. Nothing out there moves.
A signal keeper, with nobody left to pass a signal to.
The tears vanish as fast as they came. Jaeha's noisy world has been his radio.
Thirty-one seconds. The black water trembles, and a thread of violet ash rises from below.
Pim's antennae flatten. The last cold thing in here grabbed Jaeha's ankle.
So Jaeha drops the sales smile and asks what he wants.
Pim answers with a list, dramatic finger by dramatic finger. Everything on it is loud.
Item two comes with a grievance: a drama that reached him with an episode missing.
But Jaeha reads hearts the way the Call does. Festivals, dramas, crowds: everything on the list is full of people.
Item three comes out small and quiet, and it's the only one that matters.
On the breakwater, Lyra is losing patience. Borro, who answered his own Call with three seconds to spare, approves.
The timer goes red. Nine seconds.
No pitch, no smile: a modest festival, and an honest job listening to the sea.
Then he crouches to Pim's height with two seconds left, and answers item three.
Pim doesn't need the last second. He launches out of the rift, wings flaring wide, screaming with joy.
Accepted with one second to spare. Summon number four is coming through.
On the breakwater, Jaeha's eyes go dark, and a cyan slit tears open above them.
Pim falls out of it face-first, right at Lyra's boots.
Then Busan hits him: ship horns, traffic, karaoke, a beach nightclub. For ears like his, it's an avalanche.
He's in agony and in heaven at once. Lyra is charmed. Pim, with dignity, pulls rank.
Auntie Geum unties her headscarf.
She knots it over his antennae like a bonnet, and the city goes quiet for him.
In a borrowed headscarf, a hundred and forty centimetres of signal officer reports for duty.
His ears reach two hundred metres at rest, twenty kilometres in field form, and gates at any range.
Within minutes he's passing Call gossip to Lyra. A summon who hears everything also repeats it.
Across the harbour road, the same black car sits in the dark.
Han Sora's compass spins. She reports the winged newcomer, and Baek is pleased: let Jaeha do Kanghan's collecting.
Thursday, five-twenty. Jaeha is carrying ice when someone starts shouting.
Pim sprints down the aisle in an unpaid-for gaming headset, a PC bang owner and his broom right behind.
Geum stops the man dead with her ladle and settles it the market way.
Jaeha pays, and logs it like an accountant who knows his auditor.
Pim returns the headscarf, eyes closed. Forty thousand won has bought him silence.
Seoa takes the news of a fourth mouth well, until she converts the headset into kimbap.
The aunties adopt him on sight. His rank does not impress them.
Borro offers him a lettuce leaf, the highest honour Borro knows. Pim is moved to tears. Borro stays factual.
Nib stares back from his ice crate, arms folded. Pim's shy little wave gets nothing.
Pim asks Lyra about him in a whisper. Lyra, smug, explains that the stare is a feature.
At sunrise, at the end of the breakwater, a faint violet stain sits far out on the water.
Geum points the ladle at it, and Pim slides the headset down. Time to see what those ears are for.
Pim's wings open to their full span, and rings of signal ripple out across the sea.
Through LINK the sea opens up for Jaeha: every boat, the roaring city, and far out, one slow, heavy pulse.
Pim's eyes snap open. That pulse isn't a heartbeat. It's a countdown.
The window puts numbers on it: nine percent of the lid left, and three days.
Geum's steel arm twitches, and she grips it to keep it still.
Jaeha wants the alarm raised now. Geum has one person in mind, Yang, and no faith at all in Seoul.
But Pim has gone rigid, his antennae turning down toward the deep like dishes.
Down through the cracked lid, far below, hangs a violet glow: the lantern from Geum's story. Something enormous turns past it.
In Pim's eye, a tiny violet glow trembles.
And out of the deep comes a vast, broken voice, sounding out one word a syllable at a time.
It comes through the link so hard that Jaeha staggers, and his nose starts to bleed.
Pim folds his wings round himself like a blanket, shaking, and tells Jaeha the worst part.
Then a broken window he first saw in the Call flickers up. Operator number one: hushed, like the cracked bosses.
Then it breaks into cyan specks and is gone.
Jaeha wipes the blood from his lip, eyes on the sea. A man who carried before him. A lantern under the lid. And now, a number.
